whyMe.title: Why me
whyMe.text1: I love turning an idea into something people actually use.
whyMe.text2: Before coding, I worked in social services and hospitality, so I know how much simple, clear interfaces matter. I work in a structured way, think analytically and keep going until a problem is solved, ideally as part of a team.

skills.title: My Skills
skills.learningText: I keep developing my skills. Next, I am deepening my knowledge of React and Vue.js so I can join projects even more flexibly.

projects.title: My Projects
projects.organisation: How I have organised my work process

dabubble.about: DABubble is a messenger inspired by Slack. Teams chat in channels, via direct messages and in threads, all in real time.
dabubble.organisation: I split the interface into reusable Angular components and bundled the data logic in services. Clear names and short functions keep the code readable for the whole team.
dabubble.teamwork: [DRAFT] We built the app as a team of three. My tasks included the login and the channel view. We worked with Git branches and regular check-ins.

join.about: Join is a Kanban board for task management with drag and drop. In my version, n8n workflows automatically analyse incoming emails and turn them into tasks.
join.organisation: Features are split into separate files by area (board, contacts, dashboard). Data is stored in Firebase, so changes are visible to everyone instantly.
join.teamwork: [DRAFT] The base project was built as a team. Among other things, I implemented the board with drag and drop and added the email automation with n8n.

cuisine.about: Code à la Cuisine suggests recipes based on the ingredients you have in your fridge. The suggestions are generated by AI.
cuisine.organisation: I built the project type-safe with TypeScript and encapsulated the AI request in its own module so it is easy to replace.
cuisine.teamwork: [DRAFT] We divided the tasks using a Kanban board. I was responsible for the ingredient selection and the recipe view, among other things.

pollo.about: El Pollo Loco is a fun jump-and-run game: Pepe jumps over chickens, collects coins and bottles and finally faces the giant chicken.
pollo.organisation: The game is object-oriented. Every character is its own class that inherits from shared base classes. Everything is drawn on the HTML canvas.
pollo.teamwork: [DRAFT] I built this project on my own. I used feedback from code reviews to improve collision detection and animations.
